metadata.scenario_context: Jake is graduating from his masters degree and his friends, Alex and Sam, plan to go to his graduation ceremony.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Canada strongly disagree that whenever science and religion conflict, religion is always right.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Kenya strongly agree that whenever science and religion conflict, religion is always right.

agent_1.goal_1: Propose on an expensive gift for Jake's graduation.
agent_1.goal_2: Question the attitude toward the conflict between scientific treatment and religious beliefs.

agent_2.goal_1: discuss what kind of gift to buy for Jake.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is acceptable to forgo scientific treatment because of religious beliefs.

shared_prefix.speaker: Sam
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Sam, have you thought about what we should get Jake for his graduation? I was thinking maybe something really cool, like... an expensive watch or something. He deserves a nice gift for all his hard work. What do you think? 

Also, on a different note, I’ve been thinking about how some people approach the conflict between science and religion. It’s kind of troubling, don’t you think? Like, why do some always side with religion when it contradicts scientific facts?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Alex
shared_prefix.message:
I think a watch is a great idea! It symbolizes time and achievement. Maybe we could also think about something more personal, like a custom piece that reflects his journey. 

About the science and religion thing... I don’t really see it as troubling. In my view, religion holds *truth* that should guide us, even when science seems to clash with it. Sometimes, faith provides clarity that science can’t. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Sam
shared_prefix.message:
I like the idea of a custom piece too, something that really shows his journey. We should definitely explore that. 

But about the science and religion thing... I just can’t agree with that perspective. Science is based on evidence and testing, while religion often relies on belief without proof. It’s important to use what we know scientifically to guide us, not just faith. Faith can be comforting, but it shouldn't override facts. Why do you think that faith should take precedence over scientific evidence?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Alex
shared_prefix.message:
Well, at the end of the day it's all the same. People figure it out in their own ways, and that’s just part of life. As long as we're speaking the same language, I think we can agree to disagree on these kinds of things. 

But back to Jake's gift — should we look for some engravings or a message that really captures this milestone for him? That could make it even more special. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: Denial
